newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends higher on foreign stock buying.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends higher on foreign stock buying.

text.p: The won closed higher against the U.S. currency in Tuesday's hectic trading after many banks went short on the dollar on anticipation of an inflow of foreign stock funds, dealers said.
"Buying interest of Korean stocks by foreign investors seemed to be bigger than expected. This made many dealers go short from the opening bell," said a Shinhan Bank dealer.
The Securities Supervisory Board said about $600 million worth of orders came in on Tuesday, when the foreign stock limit was expanded to 20 percent from 18 percent.
The won closed at 820.70 after opening at a low of 824.50.

In the Seoul stock market, foreign investors selectively and conservatively picked up newly available shares. The composite stock index shed 0.20 point to 789.47 with an active trading volume of 66.19 million shares.
Some dealers became cautios as the dollar approached the 820 won level, the trigger mark for central bank intervention. This caused late dollar short-covering, they said.

Reflecting today's volatility, Wednesday's mid-rate forecasts ranged widely, 822.70-821.70 against today's 824.80. A Commerical Bank of Korea dealer said the dollar would move in a 819.70/821.70 range tomorrow. -- Y.J. YEOM
